description:
Redwood Inference is expanding its unified rollout system (canaries, A/B testing, rollback automation) to fully support Dedicated capacity customers who run on reserved GPU pools. Today, rollouts are largely “all-at-once” at the pool level (or rely on manual, error-prone steps), which is risky for high-SLA Dedicated tenants because a bad model/runtime/config change can saturate a reserved pool, cause queuing, and violate latency/availability commitments.

Project: “Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools” implements first-class, phased rollout controls specifically for Dedicated pools, with per-stage gates and approvals.

Goals:
- Allow operators (and eventually customers with the right permissions) to define multi-stage rollouts for Dedicated pools (e.g., Stage 0 internal shadow / Stage 1 5% / Stage 2 25% / Stage 3 100%).
- Add per-stage “gates” based on metrics and conditions (p95 latency, 5xx rate, timeouts, GPU utilization, queue depth, and optionally quality signals where available).
- Support manual approvals and automatic holds/rollbacks when gate thresholds fail.
- Ensure rollout state is auditable (who approved, what changed, when) and safe under partial failures.
- Integrate with control-plane policy evaluation and routing so traffic allocation respects stage weights and tenant isolation.

Non-goals (v1):
- Full customer self-serve for all Dedicated tenants (initially limited to Redwood operators / enterprise opt-in).
- Complex multi-armed bandit experimentation; this is deterministic staged rollout with gating (A/B remains separate but can share primitives).
- Per-request semantic quality gating for all routes (quality signals may be optional/limited to select workloads).

Key stakeholders:
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (rollout policies), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated).
- Engineering: Ethan Park (control plane), Mina Haddad (routing), Chloe Martin/Dylan Brooks (console backend), Logan Wright (telemetry), Irene Choi/Vanessa Ortiz/Keiko Yamamoto (fleet/autoscaling).
- Reliability/Operations: Sean Gallagher/Rafael Mendes/Allison Grant (SRE/observability).
- Security: Marcus Lin/Kevin Osei (auditability, RBAC).
- Customer-facing: Rachel Kim/Miguel Santos (enterprise CS), Dev Patel (support escalations).

Scope and deliverables:
1) PRD + UX flows (Console): create/edit staged rollout; view stage status; approve/abort; see gate evaluations.
2) Control plane data model: RolloutPlan, Stages, Gates, EvaluationWindow, Approval events.
3) Policy engine + routing integration: traffic weights per stage enforced deterministically; safe fallback behavior when pool is constrained.
4) Telemetry + gate evaluation service: queries and aggregation with cardinality controls; reliable “stop-the-line” behavior.
5) Operational playbooks: runbooks for paused rollouts, rollback, and incident response.
6) Beta + GA rollout: internal dogfood on Redwood-managed dedicated pools, then 2–3 enterprise customers, then general availability.

Constraints:
- Dedicated pools have strict isolation; rollout mechanisms must not cause cross-tenant interference.
- Gate evaluation must be robust to missing/late metrics; must fail safe (pause rather than proceed).
- Change management: approvals, audit logging, and minimal blast radius are required for enterprise Dedicated.

Indicative timeline (example):
- Weeks 1–2: discovery, PRD, initial design spec, alignment with Dedicated/SRE/security.
- Weeks 3–6: implement control-plane primitives + console workflows + routing integration.
- Weeks 7–8: telemetry/gates hardening, load tests, internal dogfood.
- Weeks 9–10: beta customers + operationalization; docs/runbooks.
- Week 11+: GA launch, follow-up improvements (gate types, customer self-serve, quality signals).

files.description: PRD for Dedicated staged rollouts: problem statement, target users (operators/enterprise customers), goals/non-goals, UX principles, success metrics, phased rollout plan, and open questions.
Console UX design spec: IA changes, rollout creation wizard, stage detail view, approval/abort flows, gate status visualization, and permissioning considerations.
Architecture overview for new control-plane objects (RolloutPlan/Stage/Gate), APIs, persistence, eventing, and how this integrates with existing rollout policies.
ADR choosing gate evaluation approach (server-side evaluator vs. embedded in policy engine), metric query strategy, failure modes, and rationale.
ADR on approvals model (manual approvals, roles), audit event schema, retention, and security/reliability trade-offs.
Definition of SLOs and gating thresholds for Dedicated staged rollouts (latency, error rate, queue depth), including recommended defaults and tuning guidance.
Runbook for responding to a paused rollout: how to inspect failing gates, validate metrics freshness, decide proceed vs rollback, and communication steps.
Guidance on how staged rollouts interact with reserved pools, autoscaling guardrails, and how to avoid saturating capacity during partial rollout stages.
Security doc specifying new audit log event types for staged rollouts (create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold), fields, and examples.
Dashboards/alerts spec: gate evaluation success rate, metrics latency, false-positive holds, and per-pool rollout status panels.
Beta release notes aimed at internal + select enterprise customers: feature summary, limitations, required setup, and support escalation path.
GA release notes: final behavior, API/console availability, default gates, backwards compatibility, and migration notes.
Early working draft of the PRD with brainstormed gate types, customer quotes from CS, and unresolved questions before Confluence publication.
Engineering sketch doc: proto schemas, example JSON configs, DB migration plan, and notes on idempotency/versioning.
Spike notes exploring metric availability/latency, PromQL-like query patterns, aggregation windows, and expected cardinality pitfalls.
Load test plan for staged rollouts on a reserved pool: scenarios, expected saturation points, instrumentation checklist, and pass/fail criteria.
Wireframes and iteration notes for the Console rollout UI: stage list, gate badges, approvals modal, and error states.
CS planning doc: shortlist of beta candidates, risk assessment, comms plan, required enablement, and success criteria per customer.
Draft SRE runbook with step-by-step triage flowcharts, links to dashboards, and sample incident comms templates.
Sheet-style doc (represented as tables) enumerating roles/permissions for approving/aborting rollouts across internal ops and enterprise tenants.
Launch checklist: feature flags, migrations, monitoring, internal training, documentation updates, and rollback plan.
Initiative epic: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools — milestones, beta/GA criteria, dependencies across Eng/SRE/Security/CS.
Requirement: stage definition UX + API contract (fields for weights, approval policy, evaluation windows, and default gates).
Requirement: define default gate thresholds and escalation policy for Dedicated rollouts (pause vs rollback), with SRE sign-off.
Design task: Console staged rollout workflow for Dedicated pools (wireframes, edge states, approvals UI, accessibility).
Backend: implement RolloutPlan/Stage/Gate persistence and versioned schema migrations in control plane.
API: add dedicated rollout endpoints (create/update/approve/abort/status), including idempotency and pagination for audit events.
Routing: enforce stage traffic weights for Dedicated pools; ensure deterministic allocation and tenant isolation.
Gate evaluator: service/job to evaluate gates over time windows; handle missing metrics; pause rollouts safely.
Telemetry: add metrics needed for gates (queue depth, pool utilization, timeout rate) and ensure low-cardinality dimensions.
Console backend: implement rollout orchestration APIs and websocket/polling updates for stage status.
Console frontend: build staged rollout pages, stage detail views, gate status badges, approvals modal, and error states.
Security: add audit log events for rollout actions; integrate with existing audit log export pipeline.
RBAC: permission checks for who can approve/abort rollouts; enterprise vs internal operator scopes.
Infra: integrate autoscaling guardrails with rollout stages to prevent stage-induced saturation (e.g., minimum headroom rules).
SRE: dashboards + alerts for gate evaluation health and rollout stuck/paused conditions.
Testing: end-to-end integration tests in staging: create rollout, progress stages, fail gate, auto-hold, manual approve/abort.
Docs: internal runbooks and oncall playbook updates for dedicated rollouts (pause/rollback).
Beta: enable staged rollouts for 2 pilot Dedicated customers with feature flag; capture learnings and follow-ups.
Post-GA: expand gate types (e.g., regional sub-gates, quality signals) and customer self-serve controls.
Add control-plane protobuf/schema for RolloutPlan/Stage/Gate objects; include migration scaffolding and validation rules.
Implement rollout CRUD APIs (create/update/get/list) and optimistic concurrency/versioning for dedicated rollout plans.
Add rollout approval/abort endpoints and event log (audit-style) emission; include unit tests for permission checks.
Routing integration: apply stage weights for Dedicated pools; deterministic hashing and guardrails for 0%/100% transitions.
Gate evaluator service initial implementation: evaluation loop, windowing, and pause-on-missing-metrics behavior.
Telemetry plumbing: export dedicated pool queue depth and utilization metrics required for gates; add dashboards links in code comments.
Console backend: rollout status aggregation endpoint, including stage state machine and gate evaluation summaries.
Console frontend: staged rollout list + detail page for Dedicated pools; approvals modal and abort flow.
RBAC: add new permissions (rollout.approve, rollout.abort, rollout.edit) and enforcement across APIs.
Audit logging: emit structured events for rollout actions; include actor, tenant, pool_id, plan_version, and stage id.
Fail-safe behavior: if evaluator is degraded, force rollouts into 'hold' and prevent automatic stage advancement.
Autoscaling guardrails: ensure staged rollout does not violate minimum headroom policy; add config toggles and metrics.
Add dashboards/alerts for rollout gate evaluation latency, paused rollouts, and per-pool rollout stage status.
Add perf canary scenario that simulates staged rollout traffic shifts on a reserved pool to detect regressions.
Internal-facing docs update: dedicated staged rollouts overview, API examples, and operator FAQ (mirrors Confluence content).
Integration tests: staged rollout happy path + gate fail path; include flaky-metric simulation and determinism checks.
Bugfix: stage advancement race condition when approvals arrive concurrently with evaluator tick; add locking/idempotency.
Performance: reduce cardinality in rollout/gate metrics; introduce aggregation labels and sampling for high-volume pools.
Feature flagging: enable staged rollouts for Dedicated only; per-tenant allowlist and operator override.
Add API client helpers for internal tooling (CLI/admin) to approve/abort rollouts during incidents.
